params.body:
key-1 moved onto YubiKey A on 5 October 2026 (abovebeyond-ai/abovebeyond#141), and `abovebeyond-signing.jwk` no longer exists. Until this change, `sign-mapping.mjs` read that file, so it cannot sign.

- **`sign-mapping.mjs`** opens key-1 through `scripts/key-1.mjs` in the sibling abovebeyond checkout (`ABOVEBEYOND` to point elsewhere): a PIN, then a touch per mapping. It signs as `did:web:abovebeyond.ai:id`, the successor identity, which is the only place a new key-1 is published. `did:web:abovebeyond.ai` keeps the old key-1 for good, so the mappings already in the repo still verify. The `PROVEML_CLERK_KEY` path (did:jwk, for CI) is unchanged.
- **`lib.mjs` `resolveDid`** now follows did:web paths: `did:web:host:a:b` resolves `https://host/a/b/did.json`, as the did:web spec says. Before, it always fetched `/.well-known/did.json`, so a mapping signed as `did:web:abovebeyond.ai:id` would have been checked against the old key and failed.
- **`lib.mjs` `signerFor`** also accepts an opened key with `sign(bytes)`, and gives the same base64url Ed25519 bytes as it does for a private JWK.

Checked on the workbench:
- The three committed mappings still verify through `check.mjs`.
- `did:web:abovebeyond.ai:id` resolves to the live token key; `did:web:abovebeyond.ai` still resolves to the old one.
- With one software key and a pinned clock, `issuer(privateJwk)` and `issuer(openKey(...))` produce byte-identical SD-JWTs.
- `sign-mapping.mjs` runs end to end through `key-1.mjs`, and the CI path signs and verifies as did:jwk.
- `adapters/*.test.mjs`: 23 passed.
- `npm test` points at a `test.mjs` that does not exist on `main`; that is unrelated to this change.
params.title: Sign mappings with key-1 on the token
